source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: Reciprocal verbs in Sakha and the lexicon/syntax dichotomy
notes: Some more evidence can be brought to support the lexicon/syntax division in reciprocal verbs. As shown in (58a), syntactic reciprocals cannot appear in the singular with only one argument – the subject. Lexical reciprocals, on the contrary, can. Since the with-phrase is semantically understood, it must have been saturated (existentially bound).
